The Upbot operator is installed in namespace {{ .Release.Namespace }}.

1. The operator reads the Upbot API key from a Secret{{ if .Values.upbot.apiKey }}, created by this release{{ end }}.
{{- if not .Values.upbot.apiKey }} If you haven't created it yet:

   kubectl -n {{ .Release.Namespace }} create secret generic upbot-api-key --from-literal=token=<your API key>
   kubectl -n {{ .Release.Namespace }} rollout restart deployment {{ include "upbot-operator.resourceName" (dict "suffix" "controller-manager" "context" $) }}
{{- end }}

2. Check that it runs:

   kubectl -n {{ .Release.Namespace }} get deployment {{ include "upbot-operator.resourceName" (dict "suffix" "controller-manager" "context" $) }}
   kubectl -n {{ .Release.Namespace }} logs -l control-plane=controller-manager

3. Create a monitor:

   kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
   apiVersion: monitoring.upbot.app/v1alpha1
   kind: Monitor
   metadata:
     name: example
   spec:
     type: http
     target: https://example.com
     interval: "60"
   EOF

   kubectl get monitors -A

4. Ingress watcher: {{ if .Values.upbot.ingressWatcher.enable }}on, every Ingress host gets a monitor.{{ else }}off. To create a monitor for every Ingress host:

   helm upgrade {{ .Release.Name }} <chart> -n {{ .Release.Namespace }} --reuse-values --set upbot.ingressWatcher.enable=true
{{- end }}
